result:
I've completed my investigation. Here are the answers.

---

**h01** — **`s3presign.Runner` (`RunOnce` → `CheckAndPresign`, which re-presigns S3 object URLs whose 5-day presigned link is within 4 days of expiry)** — **every 12 hours (`runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12`, `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`, ticker loop at `:29-41`), plus one immediate pass at boot** — wired in `server/server.go:162-171` (`startBackgroundRunners`: `s3presign.NewRunner(s.Store)`, `RunOnce(ctx)` at `server/server.go:163`, goroutine `Run(s3Context)` at `:169`), which is called from `Start` at `server/server.go:129`. Presign work itself: `runner.go:47-132`; expiry skip logic `runner.go:85-91`.

**h02** — Delivery function: **`webhook.Post`** — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120` (actual `safeClient.Do(req)` at `internal/webhook/webhook.go:152`); reached asynchronously via `PostAsync` (`:184`) → buffered channel + 4 worker goroutines (`:39-55`).
Protection: two layers — (1) dial-time SSRF guard `safeDialContext` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:59-77`) installed as the shared client's `Transport.DialContext` (`:32-37`), which resolves the host and rejects any reserved/private IP, defeating DNS rebinding; the reserved ranges and `isReservedIP` live in `internal/webhook/validate.go:14-54`. (2) Configuration-time validation `webhook.ValidateURL` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:62`), called when a user creates/updates a webhook (`server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go:74,161,182`). The guard can be disabled by the `--allow-private-webhooks` flag (`internal/webhook/validate.go:41`, set at `cmd/memos/main.go:49`, flag declared `cmd/memos/main.go:133`).

**h03** — Abstraction package: **`internal/idp`** (`internal/idp/idp.go:3` — shared `IdentityProviderUserInfo` contract type; the concrete config union lives in `storepb.IdentityProvider`). Implementation package: **`internal/idp/oauth2`** (`internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:20` `IdentityProvider`, constructor `:26`) — OAuth2/OIDC is the only protocol implementation shipped.

**h04** — **No.** The only construction of the MySQL driver outside the factory is none: `mysql.NewDB` is called exactly once, at `store/db/db.go:22` inside `NewDBDriver`. Evidence: `store/db/mysql` is imported by exactly one file in the repo (`store/db/db.go:8`), so no other package can construct it; within the package the only other `&DB{}` literal is in a test (`store/db/mysql/auth_config_test.go:12`). (`store/db/mysql/mysql.go:20` is the constructor itself.)

**h05** — Mechanism: **explicit Go code, in the driver-level delete-user transaction — there is no database-level rule.** Evidence:
- `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:96` `deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx` (reactions *on* the user's memos, impl `:380-388`) and `:102` `deleteReactionsByCreatorTx` (reactions *by* the user, impl `:400-403`), both inside `deleteUserTargetsTx` (`:92`) called from `DeleteUser` (`store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:29`).
- Same in the other drivers: `store/db/postgres/user_delete.go:383,401`; `store/db/mysql/user_delete.go:420,438`.
- Entry point: `store.DeleteUser` → `s.driver.DeleteUser` (`store/user.go:171-181`).
- No DB rule: the `reaction` table is declared with no foreign key/cascade in any dialect (`store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:92-99`, `store/migration/postgres/LATEST.sql:91-98`, `store/migration/mysql/LATEST.sql:91-98`); the only `ON DELETE CASCADE` in the schemas is on `memo_share.memo_id` (`store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:109` and peers).

**h06** — Handlers (all `APIV1Service` RPC methods):
- `CreateMemo` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:70` → `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` at `:157`
- `UpdateMemo` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:401` → `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` at `:513`
- `DeleteMemo` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:518` → `DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook` at `:562`
- `CreateMemoComment` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:20` → `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` at `:119`
- `SetMemoAttachments` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go:16` (→ `:48`)
- `SetMemoRelations` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go:16` (→ `:48`)

Convergence function: **`webhook.Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120`** (all paths funnel through `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook`/`DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` → `webhook.PostAsync`, `memo_service_webhooks.go:43,71` → queue workers → `Post`). Separately, `GetLinkMetadata`/`BatchGetLinkMetadata` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service_link_metadata.go:14,19`) also fetch a caller-supplied URL, but via `internal/httpgetter`, not the webhook path.

**h07**
- `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar` (route registration) — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:124`
- `(*FileServerService).serveUserAvatar` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168`
- `(*FileServerService).getUserByUsername` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715`
- `(*store.Store).GetUser` — `store/user.go:148` (in-memory `userCache` hit only when looking up by ID, so a username lookup falls through)
- `(*store.Store).ListUsers` — `store/user.go:136`
- `store.Driver.ListUsers` (interface) — `store/driver.go:47`
- `sqlite.(*DB).ListUsers` (default driver) — `store/db/sqlite/user.go:88`, selecting `avatar_url` at `store/db/sqlite/user.go:159`
- back in the handler: `parseDataURI` decodes the base64 data URI stored in `user.avatar_url` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:737`, MIME allow-list `:75-98`/`:201`, then `c.Blob` at `:207`. (The URL itself is minted by `convertUserFromStore` — `server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go:36`.)

**h08**
- `s3presign.(*Runner).RunOnce` — `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:43` — **invoked from production** — `server/server.go:163` (`startBackgroundRunners`) and self-call from `Run` at `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:36`.
- `memopayload.(*Runner).RunOnce` — `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27` — **not invoked anywhere** (no caller; `memopayload.NewRunner` is never called either — the only production use of that package is the free function `RebuildMemoPayload`, `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:107,447`). Dead code in the current wiring.

These are the only two declarations in the repo.

**h09** — **8 method declarations** named `Close` (6 non-test + 2 test), plus 2 interface method specs.
Non-test declarations: `(*SSEHub).Close` — `server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:99`; `(*Store).Close` — `store/store.go:72`; `(*cache.Cache).Close` — `store/cache/cache.go:187`; `sqlite.(*DB).Close` — `store/db/sqlite/sqlite.go:67`; `postgres.(*DB).Close` — `store/db/postgres/postgres.go:46`; `mysql.(*DB).Close` — `store/db/mysql/mysql.go:47`. Test-only: `store/test/filter_helpers_test.go:200`, `:282`. Interface specs: `store.Driver.Close` — `store/driver.go:12`; `cache.Interface.Close` — `store/cache/cache.go:31`.
Invoked by non-test server code:
- `(*Store).Close` — caller `server/server.go:146` (`Shutdown`)
- `(*SSEHub).Close` — caller `server/server.go:206` (`closeLongLivedConnections`)
- `(*cache.Cache).Close` ×3 — caller `store/store.go:74-76`
- `sqlite.(*DB).Close` — reached via the interface call `s.driver.Close()` at `store/store.go:78` (this is the one that runs on a default install; the postgres/mysql `Close` run only when that driver is selected)
Not invoked outside tests: the two `*FilterTestContext.Close`.

**h10** — **`filter.(*Engine).CompileToStatement` — `internal/filter/engine.go:74` — ~35–38 inbound call sites (34 distinct callers)**. Verified by graph fan-in and by grep (38 non-declaration call sites): production callers include `store/db/sqlite/memo_relation.go:85`, `store/db/postgres/memo_relation.go:87,98`, `store/db/mysql/memo_relation.go:78`, `server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go:413`, `server/router/api/v1/shortcut_service.go:356`, `internal/filter/helpers.go:11`, with the bulk from `store/test/*`. Runners-up: `filter.NewEngine` (33) and `filter.NewSchema` (29), `internal/filter/engine.go`/`schema.go`; `util.GenUUID` (29) `internal/util/util.go`. (Graph entries `internal.version.Len` = 179 and `internal.scheduler.Error` = 142 are resolver artifacts — misattributed builtin `len(...)` and `err.Error()` calls — `internal/version/version.go:44`, `internal/scheduler/example_test.go:89`.)

**h11** — **1st: `store.User`** (~7 packages outside the data layer: `server/auth`, `server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/router/fileserver`, `server/router/frontend`, `server/router/rss`; type at `store/user.go`). **2nd: `store.Memo`** (~6: `server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/router/frontend`, `server/router/rss`, `server/runner/memopayload`; type at `store/memo.go`). Next is `store.Attachment` (~4). Counts from `store.<Type>` references excluding `store/**` itself.

**h12** — Concrete method: **`sqlite.(*DB).CreateMemo` — `store/db/sqlite/memo.go:16`, with the `INSERT INTO memo ... RETURNING ...` executed at `store/db/sqlite/memo.go:41-47`**.
Determination: the `driver` setting defaults to `"sqlite"` (`cmd/memos/main.go:122` `viper.SetDefault`, flag default `cmd/memos/main.go:130`), and is read into `Profile.Driver` at `cmd/memos/main.go:43`; `db.NewDBDriver` switches on it and returns `sqlite.NewDB(profile)` (`store/db/db.go:18-20`, constructor `store/db/sqlite/sqlite.go:24` returning `store.Driver = &DB{}`); `store.New(dbDriver, …)` stores it (`cmd/memos/main.go:63`, `store/store.go:38-58`); the API layer's `s.Store.CreateMemo` delegates through the interface at `store/memo.go:113` (`s.driver.CreateMemo`), and the interface method is declared at `store/driver.go:29`. So the three candidate implementations (`sqlite`/`postgres`/`mysql` `memo.go`) are selected purely by that flag, and sqlite wins by default.

**h13** — Impl: **exactly one — the unexported `*markdown.service`** (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:58-60`, implementing the `Service` interface declared at `internal/markdown/markdown.go:31-55`; e.g. `ExtractAll` at `:356` is the only implementation of that method in the repo).
Construction: `markdown.NewService(...)` — `internal/markdown/markdown.go:85` — called once in production at `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:48` (with `WithTagExtension()` and `WithMentionExtension()`), and in tests at `server/router/api/v1/test/test_helper.go:44`.
Holders of the interface: `APIV1Service.MarkdownService` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:35`), `rss.RSSService.MarkdownService` (`server/router/rss/rss.go:45`, injected from the API service at `server/server.go:84`), `memopayload.Runner.MarkdownService` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:16`) and the `RebuildMemoPayload` parameter (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74`).

**h14** — Computation site: **`memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload` — `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74-88`**, which delegates to `MarkdownService.ExtractAll` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:356`) and assigns `memo.Payload.Tags` and `memo.Payload.Property` (`runner.go:85-86`).
Triggers: `CreateMemo` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:107`), `UpdateMemo` on a content change (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:447`), and the bulk backfill `memopayload.(*Runner).RunOnce` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27,52`) — which is currently not wired into startup.
Extracted properties: deduplicated `#tags` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:380-382,419-420`) and `MemoPayload_Property` = `Title` (text of a leading H1, `:384-390`), `HasLink` (`:394`), `HasCode` (code block/fence/span, `:397`), `HasTaskList` and `HasIncompleteTasks` (unchecked task checkbox, `:399-405`). `Mentions` are also produced by the same walk (`:383-385`) but consumed for notifications rather than stored in the payload. Note the list/preview *snippet* is a separate, read-time derivation: `getMemoContentSnippet` → `GenerateSnippet` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:83`, `internal/markdown/markdown.go:264`).

**h15** — Distinct memo-visibility enforcement sites:
- `checkMemoReadAccess` (single-memo read gate; used by `GetMemo`, comment listing) — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:39-67` (callers `:356`, `:367`, `memo_service_comments.go:148`)
- `ListMemos` visibility scoping of the query (`VisibilityList` / `creator_id || visibility in [...]` filter) — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:217-227`
- `UpdateMemo`/`DeleteMemo` creator-or-admin write gate — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:409-411` region and `:540-542`
- `CreateMemoComment` parent-memo gate — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:41`
- `checkAttachmentAccess` (gRPC attachment surface, derives from parent memo visibility) — `server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go:422-455` (esp. `:445,451`)
- `ListMemoAttachments` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go:213-225`
- Reaction service (`UpsertMemoReaction` / delete) — `server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go:30-40` and `:83`
- `checkAttachmentPermission` (native HTTP file server, incl. share-token bypass) — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:650-705` (esp. `:677`, `:699`)
- SSE delivery filter `(*SSEClient).canReceive` — `server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:134-143` (applied in `Broadcast`, `:125`)
- RSS feeds restricted to `store.Public` — `server/router/rss/rss.go:90` (`GetExploreRSS`) and `:141` (`GetUserRSS`)
- Sitemap restricted to `store.Public` — `server/router/frontend/frontend.go:150`
- User memo stats scoping — `server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go:84-90` and `:218-220`
- Mention/comment notification gating — `server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go:62-84`, `server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go:309-312`, `server/notification/email.go:313-316`
- Share-token surface that deliberately bypasses visibility (token + expiry + archived check instead) — `server/router/api/v1/memo_share_service.go:153-170`, `getActiveMemoShare` `:199`

**r01** — Premise is wrong: **there is no Redis anywhere in this codebase** (a case-insensitive search for `redis` across all Go/config files returns nothing, and it is not in `go.mod`). The cache layer is a **process-local in-memory cache**: `store/cache/cache.go` (`Cache` struct `:66`, `sync.Map` + TTL per item, background `cleanupLoop` started in `New` `:76-85`). Three instances are created in `store.New` — `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache` (`store/store.go:27-29`, `:51-53`) — all sharing one config: **`DefaultTTL = 10 minutes`**, `CleanupInterval = 5 minutes`, `MaxItems = 1000` (`store/store.go:40-45`; identical defaults at `store/cache/cache.go:57-63`). So user entries expire 10 minutes after being `Set` (`store/user.go:143`, `:167`), and are invalidated eagerly on update/delete (`store/user_delete.go:39-47`). Caches are torn down in `(*Store).Close` (`store/store.go:74-76`).

**r02** — Premise is wrong: **there is no rate-limiting middleware in this codebase.** The only Echo middleware registered on the server is `middleware.Recover()` and the CORS middleware (`server/server.go:51-52`), plus static-file/SPA-fallback middleware in the frontend service (`server/router/frontend/frontend.go:54,59`). The Connect/gRPC interceptor chain contains only metadata, logging and panic-recovery interceptors (`server/router/api/v1/connect_interceptors.go:22,98,164`) plus the auth/ACL authorizer (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:66-88`, `authz.go`). The only occurrence of the phrase "rate limit" in the repo is an aspirational comment about email sending (`internal/email/doc.go:86`). Related-but-different real limits: concurrency semaphores for thumbnails/image processing (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:57-58`, `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:117`), a batch-size cap on link metadata (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service_link_metadata.go:23`), and a 128-entry bounded webhook queue (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`).

**r03** — Premise is wrong: **there is no cron scheduler running any jobs, and no nightly database-cleanup job at all.** A cron *library* exists at `internal/scheduler` (`scheduler.go`, `parser.go`, `job.go`, `middleware.go`), but it is imported only by its own tests — `internal/scheduler/example_test.go:10` and `internal/scheduler/integration_test.go:13` — so nothing in the server registers a job with it (no non-test reference to `scheduler.New`/`Register`, and no `cron` reference outside that package). The only scheduled background work is the S3 presign runner on a 12-hour `time.Ticker` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27-41`, started at `server/server.go:162-171`) and the caches' 5-minute cleanup loops (`store/cache/cache.go:76`, interval `store/store.go:42`) — none of them time-of-day based, and none of them a DB cleanup.

**r04** — Premise is wrong: **there is no message broker — neither NATS nor RabbitMQ appears in the codebase, and no queue is declared in any broker.** Webhook delivery is entirely in-process: a package-level **buffered Go channel** `asyncPostQueue = make(chan *WebhookRequestPayload, 128)` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`) with **4 worker goroutines** started in `init()` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-55`), each calling `Post` (`:46`). Producers call `webhook.PostAsync` (`:184`), which does a non-blocking send and **drops** the payload with a warning when the buffer is full (`:189-195`). Consequences worth noting: the queue is unpersisted, so pending deliveries are lost on restart, and there are no retries.

**r05** — Premise is wrong: **there is no GraphQL schema or GraphQL server anywhere** (no match for `graphql` in any `.go`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, or `.proto` file). The public API is **protobuf/Connect-RPC defined in `proto/api/v1/*.proto`** (generated code in `proto/gen/api/v1`, Connect handlers in `proto/gen/api/v1/apiv1connect`), exposed three ways: gRPC-Gateway REST + Connect handlers registered by `(*APIV1Service).RegisterGateway` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:66`, services wired in `server/router/api/v1/connect_services.go`, `connect_handler.go`), plus non-RPC HTTP surfaces — the file server `/file/...` (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:121-125`), RSS (`server/router/rss/rss.go:67`), an MCP endpoint (`server/router/mcp/service.go`, OpenAPI catalog in `openapi.go`), SSE (`server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go`), and `/healthz` (`server/server.go:69`).
